title: The Preposition Vehicle Rule (In vs On)
poem_verse:
You get IN a car, you get IN a cab,
Where you sit down low and hail with a grab.
You get IN a helicopter, helicopter, truck, or van,
Where you crouch down small as tight as you can!

But you get ON a bus, and you get ON a train,
ON a ship, ON a ferry, or ON an airplane!
If you can stand up and walk down the floor,
Use ON for your ride right out the door!
the_rule_explained: Use 'IN' for small private enclosed vehicles where you cannot walk upright (in a car, in a taxi). Use 'ON' for larger public transport or open platforms where you can physically stand and walk (on a bus, on a train, on a plane, on a ship, on a bicycle).
bengali_mentor_tip: Bengali uses a single locative case marker '-e' / '-te' (গাড়িতে, বাসে) for both situations. In English, you must distinguish between sitting trapped ('in') vs boarding a walking deck ('on').
quick_quiz: Fill in the blank: 'After waiting for thirty minutes at the terminal, we finally got [ ___ ] the intercity bus.' (Answer: ON)

title: The 'I Agree' Limerick
poem_verse:
A student once spoke with a confident plea,
"Dear examiner, sir, I am totally agree!"
The examiner sighed with a sorrowful frown,
And ticked off a point as the mark went right down!
Remember the verb needs no 'am' to be free:
Say 'I firmly concur' or just say 'I AGREE!'
the_rule_explained: 'Agree' is already a verb in English. It does not require the auxiliary 'am'. You say 'I agree', 'I disagreed', or 'I have agreed'.
bengali_mentor_tip: Bengali speakers translate 'ami ekmot' (where 'ekmot' feels like an adjective) into 'I am agree'. Always treat 'agree' as an action verb!
quick_quiz: Which sentence is grammatically correct? A) 'I am agree with the author.' B) 'I agree with the author.' (Answer: B)

title: The 'Discuss About' Preposition Banisher
poem_verse:
When talking of problems or matters of clout,
Never say that you're going to 'discuss about'!
For 'discuss' takes its object directly and clean:
'Let's discuss the dilemma,' is what you should mean!

The same goes for 'order'—don't 'order for tea',
Just 'order a cup' and be happy and free!
the_rule_explained: Transitive verbs like 'discuss', 'order', 'reach', and 'emphasize' take a direct object without prepositions. Never say 'discuss about the essay' or 'ordered for food'.
bengali_mentor_tip: In Bengali, we say 'eta niye alochona kora' ('about this discuss'). In English, 'discuss' already incorporates the 'about'.
quick_quiz: Correct this sentence: 'In this essay, I will discuss about the environmental impacts.' (Correct: 'In this essay, I will discuss the environmental impacts.')

title: The Third Conditional Regret Song
poem_verse:
If you had revised with devotion and care,
You would have succeeded without a despair!
Remember the past that can never return,
Takes HAD and PAST PARTICIPLE—listen and learn!

In the consequence clause, put WOULD HAVE and DONE,
And your Band 8 complexity battle is won!
the_rule_explained: Third conditional expresses past counter-factuals (regrets or alternate history): 'If + had + past participle, ... would have + past participle'.
bengali_mentor_tip: Bengali speakers often use 'If I would study, I would pass'. In English, never put 'would' in the 'if' condition clause!
quick_quiz: Complete the sentence: 'If local authorities [ ___ ] (build) the embankment sooner, the floodwaters [ ___ ] (not destroy) the village.' (Answer: had built / would not have destroyed)

title: The Inversion Drama Spell
poem_verse:
Seldom have I witnessed such glorious sight,
Rarely do scholars surrender the fight!
Not only did technology quicken the pace,
But it also transformed the whole human race!

When negative adverbs begin your bold line,
Swap auxiliary and subject to make your text shine!
the_rule_explained: Negative and restrictive adverbs (Seldom, Rarely, Never, Scarcely, Not only, Little) at the beginning of a sentence trigger question word order (auxiliary verb + subject + main verb).
bengali_mentor_tip: Using one accurate inversion in IELTS Writing Task 2 or Speaking Part 3 instantly signals a Band 8.5+ command of grammatical range to the examiner.
quick_quiz: Invert this sentence: 'Governments rarely invest in preventive healthcare.' (Answer: 'Rarely do governments invest in preventive healthcare.')

title: The 'Stationary vs Stationery' Rhyme
poem_verse:
Station-ERY with an E is for Envelope and pen,
The paper and ink that you write with again!
While station-ARY with an A means staying in place,
Like a car at red lights that is paused in its space!
the_rule_explained: Stationery (with an E) = writing materials (envelopes, pens). Stationary (with an A) = not moving, fixed in place.
bengali_mentor_tip: Spelling errors in IELTS Listening Section 1 cost full marks! Remember: 'E' is for Envelope!
quick_quiz: Fill in: 'The train remained [ ___ ] on the platform for ten minutes.' (Answer: stationary)

title: The 'Affect vs Effect' Battle
poem_verse:
Affect with an A is an Action you start,
An active verb moving straight to the heart!
Effect with an E is the End result shown,
The noun or outcome that clearly is known!

Heavy rain can AFFECT your commute on the train,
And traffic congestion's the common EFFECT of the rain!
the_rule_explained: Affect is predominantly a Verb (to influence). Effect is predominantly a Noun (the result/consequence). Remember RAVEN: Remember Affect Verb Effect Noun.
bengali_mentor_tip: Bengali speakers often mix these up in Writing Task 2. Look at the word before it: if it follows 'the' or 'an', it MUST be 'effect'!
quick_quiz: Choose the correct word: 'Pollution has a detrimental [affect/effect] on marine biodiversity.' (Answer: effect)

title: The Preposition of Time Triangle (At, On, In)
poem_verse:
AT is the point, like a clock on the wall,
At noon, at five-thirty, at night when stars fall!
ON is the day, on a Tuesday so bright,
On dates, on my birthday, on weekends in sight!
IN is the season, the month, and the year,
In summer, in August, in centuries near!

From specific to broad as the pyramid climbs:
AT the hour, ON the day, IN the seasons and times!
the_rule_explained: AT = precise point in time (at 5 PM, at midnight). ON = specific days and calendar dates (on Monday, on July 14th). IN = longer periods (in June, in 2026, in the 21st century, in winter).
bengali_mentor_tip: Don't say 'in Monday' or 'at 2024'. Follow the pyramid: Point (At) -> Line/Day (On) -> Space/Year (In).
quick_quiz: Fill in: 'The lecture will begin [ ___ ] 9:00 AM [ ___ ] Monday morning.' (Answer: at / on)

title: The 'Since vs For' Timeline Chant
poem_verse:
SINCE marks the start when the clock started ticking:
Since Monday, since morning, since childhood began!
FOR counts the span of the time that is kicking:
For three days, for ten years, for as long as a man!

Since tells the origin, crystal and plain,
For counts the duration of pleasure or pain!
the_rule_explained: Use 'SINCE' with a specific starting point in time (since 2015, since yesterday, since graduating). Use 'FOR' with a measurable duration of time (for 5 hours, for two decades).
bengali_mentor_tip: Avoid the common Bengali error: 'I am living in Dhaka since five years.' Correct: 'I have been living in Dhaka for five years.'
quick_quiz: Fill in: 'She has been practicing for the IELTS exam [ ___ ] six consecutive months.' (Answer: for)

title: The 'Complement vs Compliment' Distiction

"Your spoken test fluency sets you apart!"
While compl-E-ment with an E means to complete and enhance,
Like wine and good cheese in a flavorful dance!
the_rule_explained: Compliment (with 'i') = words of praise or admiration. Complement (with 'e') = something that completes or goes well with something else.
bengali_mentor_tip: Remember: 'I' love receiving a compl'I'ment!
quick_quiz: Choose: 'The new subway line serves as an essential [complement/compliment] to the existing bus routes.' (Answer: complement)
